sections.html:
Up in northern Davis County, Syracuse stretches between the Great Salt Lake's east shore and Interstate 15, about 30 miles from Salt Lake City. The city spans around 10 square miles and sits at 4,272 feet. West Point is to the north, Clearfield to the east and northeast, and Layton to the southeast. A causeway off State Route 127 links the city to Antelope Island State Park, and Syracuse bills itself the Gateway to Antelope Island.

Buyers like the lake and island access. The land on the west side has wetlands that limit what can be built there.

Population climbed from 4,658 in 1990 to 9,398 in 2000, 24,331 in 2010 and 32,141 in 2020, and the estimate for July 1, 2025 is 39,909. About 89.7% of homes are owner-occupied, households average 3.64 people, and the 2020 to 2024 median value is $573,300. Treat that as a survey midpoint rather than a price for your place. With so much of the housing built during the boom, the ages of the roof, water heater and furnace tell buyers more than the neighborhood's age.

The West Davis Corridor, State Route 177, opened on January 6, 2024. It runs northwest through Syracuse with interchanges at 2000 West and Antelope Drive. The first section is 16 miles long, from Farmington to West Point, and cost $750 million.

The highway reshaped travel on the county's west side and drew interest to the land beside it. Syracuse is pursuing a 169-acre redevelopment area, the WDC Gateway Community Reinvestment Area, at Antelope Drive and 3000 West, for housing, retail and commercial use. City staff say interest rose sharply after the opening. Most of that ground is farmed or undeveloped and needs wetland mitigation, a hurdle the city describes as significant. UDOT plans a 2.5-mile extension north to 1800 North in West Point, with work running through 2027.

New building nearby can help or hurt a sale depending on who is looking. A cash buyer values the house as it is today.

Summers run hot and winters are real. Highs often hit 95 degrees, yearly totals average about 24 inches of precipitation and 39 inches of snow, and monsoon storms roll in from late July to mid-September. Gutters, roofs and grading get punished, and freezing and thawing wears on older decks, driveways and sprinkler lines.

  • Check the roof and flashing after winter and after monsoon season.
  • Look at grading near the foundation, because snowmelt and rain need somewhere to go.
  • Have the sprinkler lines blown out each fall before a hard freeze.

The Davis School District serves Syracuse, and the Syracuse Arts Academy charter campuses are public schools with separate enrollment. Syracuse High School opened in 2007, Syracuse Junior High dates to 1960, and elementary schools include Cook (1979), Syracuse Elementary (1968), Bluff Ridge (1999) and Buffalo Point (2008). Boundaries are the first thing families ask, so check yours ahead of listing.

sections.h2: Garage sales and home business rules
sections.html:
City code chapter 10.35 governs home businesses and temporary sales, which comes into play when you are emptying a house. A garage or yard sale needs no license for up to three consecutive days, and you can hold up to four such events a year.

  • Minor home occupations are allowed in residential zones if they use no more than 300 square feet or 20% of the floor area.
  • Home occupation permits are not transferable and end when the applicant stops living at the address, so a buyer must apply again.
  • A business license is required unless the business is exempt under state law.

If you run a daycare, salon or similar business from the house, tell the buyer the permit does not carry over. For anything else, contact Syracuse City planning for current rules.

sections.h2: Davis County property taxes and appeals
sections.html:
Payment is due November 30, shifting to the next business day when that lands on a weekend or holiday. After it, the penalty is 2.5% or $10, whichever is more. A primary residence gets Utah's 45% exemption, up to one acre.

StepTiming
Valuation notice mailedEnd of July
Appeal to the county Board of EqualizationBy September 15 each year, so file early
Taxes dueNovember 30
Late penalty2.5% or $10, whichever is greater

An appeal covers market value only, never the tax rate. Acceptable evidence includes closing documents, a certified appraisal, three or more comparable sales, or proof the assessor's data is wrong. Visit Tax Administration at 61 South Main Street, Room 101, Farmington, or call 801-451-3331.

Owing tax will not end a sale, though it must be cleared at closing. The title company gets the balance from the county, subtracts it from what you receive, and shares the current year with the buyer. Tell the title officer about any delinquency first thing. Should the valuation seem high, the September 15 appeal date stays open during escrow, and a lower value shrinks your portion of the tax.

sections.h2: What to bring to a Syracuse closing
sections.html: Pack photo ID, a lender payoff statement for any mortgage, your most recent tax notice, permit papers for basement finishes or additions, and all keys, garage openers and gate codes. A home occupation permit at the address ends when you leave, so say so. Empty the garage and yard before the last walk-through, and if you want to sell belongings, the three-day sale allowance can help.

People who call us are typically on a clock: relocating for work, divorcing, outgrowing the house, or holding an inherited property no one wants. Updated, spotless houses do well on the market. If yours needs work, or you would rather skip showings and the wait, a cash offer gives you an easy point of comparison.

Our purchases are as-is, and you set the closing date. Get the offer, put it beside a listing's net after commissions and repairs, and decline if the numbers fall short. The title company arranges payoffs and the tax split, and the remainder is yours at signing.

faqs.q: How many people live in Syracuse, Utah?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 39,909 residents as of July 1, 2025. The 2020 census counted 32,141, so the city grew by more than 7,000 people in five years.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Syracuse, Utah?
faqs.a: The median value of owner-occupied homes is $573,300 for 2020 to 2024. That is a survey estimate, not an appraisal of your house.

faqs.q: When are Davis County property taxes due?
faqs.a: November 30. If that date falls on a weekend or holiday, it moves to the next business day. After it, a penalty of 2.5% or $10, whichever is greater, applies.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Syracuse property valuation?
faqs.a: Yes. Davis County mails valuation notices at the end of July, and appeals are due by September 15. You can appeal only the market value, with evidence such as comparable sales or an appraisal.

faqs.q: Do I need a license for a garage sale in Syracuse?
faqs.a: No license is needed for up to three consecutive days, with a limit of four events per year, under city code chapter 10.35.
